title: 015 · f and f′ together: the slope is 0 at every peak and valley (NDA maths concept, predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Derivatives. At the top of the hill, the slope graph is…? A highest · B zero · C lowest 👇

Slide a tangent along f(x) = x³ − 3x and draw its slope below: f′(x) = 3x² − 3.
At every peak and valley the tangent is flat, so f′ = 0 → B. That's how you find maxima and minima: solve f′(x) = 0.
Trap: f″ < 0 at a peak isn't guaranteed (−x⁴ has a peak at 0 with f″(0) = 0).
NDA asked this idea in 2024 (I), Q91.
